points.text: Theorem is a Gaussian toy model where infinite weight norm trivially dominates; irrelevant to trained MoEs
Gaussian hidden-state assumption justified only by a blog notebook citation
KL expression in Eq. 9 inconsistent and Definition 1 not meaningful
Extension of theory to more experts only asserted in one sentence
Theory not connected to actual fine-tuning mechanism; 'theoretical foundation' overstated
Implementation inconsistent with method: unclear whether LoRA on attention or dormant experts trained
Baselines may get fewer trainable parameters; missing matched-parameter, optimized-trigger control
Ablations show dormant-expert selection adds about one ASR point; architectural claim undemonstrated
Baselines appear poorly tuned (near-zero Samsum, chance-level IMDB ASR)
Single run reported with no variance or seeds
No measurement of whether triggered inputs actually route to dormant experts
Only one layer attacked; trigger effect at other layers untested
t-SNE evidence qualitative; no inference-time expert ablation to verify control
Token-ID routing and query-independence not verified; position/context sensitivity not shown
Clean baseline is untuned base model; clean fine-tuned comparison missing
Substantial side-effect degradation on unrelated tasks; no standard benchmarks like MMLU
Stealthiness expert-usage measure cannot detect modified dormant experts
Defense evaluation lacks MoE-specific defenses (expert pruning, weight diffing) and trigger-inversion/scanning
ONION resistance expected given perplexity-constrained trigger
Fine-tuning resistance not tested for other tasks, hyperparameters or router/expert tuning
Abstract claim of >80% ASR under defenses holds only for subset of settings
Hidden-state separability defense evaluated on one model and dataset
Trigger stealthiness overstated: poisoned-input perplexities very high
Trigger naturalness not evaluated by humans or detectors; trigger text not shown
Threat model identical to dense backdoors; routing-based triggers unnecessary
Stealth from dormant experts not tested against adaptive defender
Only base models, simple targets; no instruction-tuned, chat or larger MoEs
Prompt-format robustness only partial; AGNews ASR drops 25 points
Template headers, typos and misattributed citations
Code and data released only upon acceptance; not reproducible now
Many key details placed in appendices
'First MoE backdoor' claim not checked against concurrent work
Dominating expert definition ignores other experts
Theorem 4.1 trivial: large enough additive output dominates others
Infection step trains much of model; unclear how much remains untrained
Training objective symmetric; nothing enforces stated roles of theta_0 and theta_a
MoE-specific defenses not explored; dormant expert pruning discussion shallow
Persistence under domain adaptation or large-scale instruction tuning not assessed
Limited evidence attack is feasible in real model supply chains with upload verification
No demonstration in complete deployment pipeline such as hosted API
Persistence under model updates or reinforcement fine-tuning unclear
Utility evaluation sparse; should use standard LLM benchmarks
Clean accuracy untested on tasks where dormant experts are actually active
Gaussian assumption unrealistic given activation outliers in LLMs
Attack components do not leverage Theorem 4.1; loss is standard backdoor loss
Results only incrementally better than prior baselines
Motivation weak: framed mainly as not done before
Simple per-expert testing defenses could easily fix the attack
Unclear whether attack works on MoEs with many fine-grained experts like DeepSeek
